cards.text: The prophet Ezekiel says the word of the LORD came to him in the eleventh year, on the first day of the third month. God tells him to speak to Pharaoh king of Egypt and to his multitude, and the message opens with a question: "Who can be compared to your greatness?" Friend, in the junk drawer, people just held me up and asked what on earth I was.

cards.question: God tells Pharaoh to look at a nation pictured as a cedar in Lebanon. Which nation is it?

cards.text: And WHAT a cedar: beautiful branches shading the forest, its top way up among the clouds. Friend, this tree doesn't have a top. It has a weather forecast.

cards.question: What does God say made the great cedar grow so tall?

cards.text: With all that water, it towers higher than all the trees of the field, and its boughs grow long. This is the guy who gets sent to the back row of EVERY group photo.
And everybody wants a spot. All the birds of the air nest in its branches, and all the beasts of the field give birth beneath its boughs.

cards.question: All the great nations lived in the cedar's ___.
The cedars in the garden of God could rival this great cedar.

cards.text: This cedar is the envy of all the trees of Eden, in the garden of God. Every one of them is looking at it like the coworker who just got the corner office.

cards.question: God says the great cedar made itself beautiful.

cards.text: After all that praise for the great cedar, the word "Therefore" shows up. You know when a performance review is ALL compliments and you can FEEL the "however" coming?

cards.question: After all that praise, what does God hold against the great cedar?

answers.text: It grew proud of its height
It drank up all the water

cards.text: So God delivers it into the hand of the ruler of the nations, to deal with it according to its wickedness. Then God says, "I have banished it."
Foreigners, the most ruthless of the nations, cut it down and leave it, with its branches fallen on the mountains and in every valley. TIMBERRR.

cards.question: After the great cedar is cut down, all the peoples of the earth stay in its shade.
The birds of the air used to nest in the great cedar's branches. Where do they nest now that it's down?
God says the great cedar was cut down so other trees could grow even taller.

cards.text: And God says those trees have all been consigned to death, to the depths of the earth, among the mortals who descend to the Pit. Friend, I thought the back of a junk drawer was low, but that's a WHOLE other basement.
On the day the cedar is brought down to Sheol, God causes mourning and holds back its rivers. All that water that made it the tallest tree around, friend, SHUT OFF like a hose somebody stepped on.

cards.question: God makes Lebanon mourn for the fallen cedar. What happens to all the trees of the field?
God made the nations ___ at the sound of the cedar's downfall.
Down in the earth below, all the trees of Eden are consoled. They went down to Sheol with the great cedar too. Who were they to the cedar?

cards.text: Then God turns back to Pharaoh with a question a lot like the one He opened with: "Who then is like you in glory and greatness among the trees of Eden?"

cards.question: God tells Pharaoh that he will be brought down to the depths of the earth too, to lie with those slain by the sword.

cards.text: Then God spells it out: "This is Pharaoh and all his multitude, declares the Lord GOD." So the one that compares with Pharaoh's greatness is a giant tree lying in pieces, and I bet that's NOT the compliment he was fishing for.
